Also restructures how the secp256k1 signing and verification contexts are owned and initialized, decoupling that lifecycle from key.h.

result.summary: This PR plugs Bitcoin Core's own hardware-optimized SHA256 compression function into libsecp256k1's context, so ECDSA and Schnorr signing use the SHA-NI/ARMv8/SSE4 implementation instead of libsecp's bare internal one. Along the way it restructures ECC_Context to own both a signing and a new verification context, decouples ECC initialization from key.h/pubkey.h, and moves ECC_Context into the consensus library so it can eventually live in the kernel. It updates all call sites (fuzz targets, benchmarks, bitcoin-tx, bitcoin-wallet) to the new context API and adds a benchmark and a unit test for the new lifecycle.
result.problem: libsecp256k1 previously used its own internal SHA256, missing Bitcoin Core's hardware-accelerated implementation, so ECDSA and Schnorr signing (the hot path for wallets and PSBT signing) ran slower than necessary. Since secp256k1 PR #1777 upstream allows an externally supplied SHA256 compression function, this closes that gap.

categories.rationale: Description reports measured gains: 'ECDSASign 79.2us to 69.3us (-13%), SchnorrSign 39.9us to 37.1us (-7%)' on ARM64 SHA-NI hardware, a durable performance improvement to a widely used primitive. It also cleans up global crypto-context ownership (a correctness-adjacent area per the category's own priorities) and creates a verification context that unblocks further decoupling work, though the change is internal plumbing rather than a new user feature.

uncertainties: Whether real-or-random (cc'd by fanquake) will raise substantive concerns about the libsecp integration once they weigh in, which could shift Agreement.
Whether the kernel-library membership deserves higher priority once the project's kernel decoupling roadmap is checked; treated here as supporting groundwork rather than a kernel API milestone.
No explicit security review yet of the new context-ownership and deleter mechanics (unique_ptr with custom deleter, no-copy ECC_Context), though no bug has been reported.
result.card: This PR plugs Bitcoin Core's hardware-optimized SHA256 into libsecp256k1's signing and verification contexts, using a new upstream libsecp capability, giving a measured ~13% ECDSA signing and ~7% Schnorr signing speedup on SHA-NI hardware. It also restructures ECC_Context lifecycle management, decoupling it from key.h/pubkey.h and moving it into the consensus library as groundwork for the kernel decoupling project. Six members gave concept ACKs (w0xlt, fjahr, sedited, ismaelsadeeq, theStack, hebasto) with no objections, and fanquake has cc'd real-or-random for further input. The PR is ready for review now with clean CI and no rebase needed. Its main value is in utils (signing performance and context-management cleanup) with secondary, smaller value in kernel (library decoupling groundwork).
